Texans vs Colts 🐴 🔵

1. The Texans Pass Catchers vs the Colts Passing Defense 🔵

Here’s how the Texans’ pass catchers have matched up against Cover 1/2/3 this season:

If I had to pick a Texans pass catcher to have a big game in this matchup, it would be Tank Dell, based on his success against 1-high coverage so far this year and the Colts’ inability to defend the slot.

2. The Colts Pass Catchers vs the Texans Passing Defense 🐴

Before diving into the coverage matchup, it’s important to note that the Colts will be without their two starting tackles (Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis). If I had to pick a Colts pass catcher to thrive in this matchup, it would be Laquon Treadwell based on the amount of routes he’s likely to run and the Texans’ vulnerability to explosive plays. (Treadwell has a 15.58 aDOT against Cover 3/6 this year.)

3. David Montgomery vs the Colts Rush Defense 🔵

Lou Anarumo’s defense has really struggled to stop the run this season, ranking 28th in EPA/rush allowed (−0.01), 26th in rushing success rate allowed (42.6%), 29th in yards per carry allowed (4.75), and 26th in yards before contact per attempt allowed (1.65). Additionally, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 29th in the NFL in run-block win rate. So the Colts’ run defense should be able to hold up to some extent in this matchup. As far as rush concepts go, 57.7% of David Montgomery’s rush attempts this year have come on man/gap concepts. The Colts defense has been okay defending man/gap concepts, allowing 4.28 yards per carry and a 48.7% success rate. Overall, Montgomery’s success in this game will depend on the game script. (Woody Marks is also out with a concussion.)

4. Jonathan Taylor/Seth McGowan vs the Texans Run Defense 🐴

Since Week 6, the Texans’ rush defense has been atrocious, ranking 27th in EPA/rush allowed (0.01), 31st in rushing success rate allowed (47.4%), and 25th in yards per carry allowed (4.66). This is significant because the Texans’ defense has been much better against zone concepts than man/gap concepts. DeMeco Ryans’ defense is allowing just 3.62 yards per carry against zone concepts compared to 4.62 against man/gap. With the Colts’ offensive line banged up, I don’t see how their offense will be able to move the football efficiently in this game.

Additionally, the Bills have a game on deck on Thanksgiving, so I’m not expecting Joe Brady to run Josh Allen much in this matchup. There’s also a chance Kyle Allen takes some knees at the end of this game.

So I’m expecting Jared Goff to operate in a clean pocket for the most part in this game, which sets up Jameson Williams to catch a deep ball. Against Cover 3 this year, Williams owns a 17.35 ADOT along with a 38.7% air-yard share. (The Bucs defense has run Cover 3 at the highest rate in the NFL this season at 51.8%.) In a game where the Lions run game will likely be neutralized, I’m expecting Jameson Williams to catch at least one deep ball.

- Purdy threw a number of passes with anticipation to a spot to Mike Evans and George Kittle, which made a lot of sense given who they were playing. By a spot, in this specific sense, I mean Purdy gave both of them targets in the first half that required maximum confidence in his pass catcher.

- The 49ers pass protection was fantastic given the opponent they faced, but Purdy also had a great game in pressure management.

- Mike Tirico said this, but the brotherhood aspect of the Colton McKivitz injury said a lot about the 49ers as a team, and it was a fine example of both what’s wonderful about football, as well as the uncomfortable downside.

- I will write something 49ers specific tomorrow.

- For the Vikings, I’m not surprised their offensive line had issues with that 49ers front, that group is the primary reason they showed out as a tier below the 49ers tonight.

- I did not hate Kirk Cousins game, especially considering he was on a different team two weeks ago. I thought there was more good than bad in a tough situation.

- Justin Jefferson not only had the brutal, very poorly timed fumble, but for a while now I’m left wanting more.

- I actually thought T.J. Hockenson had a solid game, but it also looked like Minnesota needed a second option in their passing game tonight. Addison is sidelined, and while Jauan Jennings has never been a great player, even during the year he saw a ton of volume in San Francisco, he’s been a complete non-factor as a Viking.

- The 49ers also scored on defense with a Ji’Ayir Brown pick six.

Bears 21, Saints 13
- Bears were up 16-0, but the Saints clawed back in built off a long run from Travis Etienne and another on a later drive from Tyler Shough. The game was mostly a defensive/ ugly offense contest from there.

- The Bears defense won this game, and Dennis Allen is Ben Johnson’s Steve Spagnualo, which was on full display today.

- Jeffery Simmons was a real problem in this game, finishing with 3 sacks and several other disruptive reps. If he started the season with Chicago, he might have been this year’s Defensive Player of the Year, and he’s probably not drawing dead at it anyway given how well he’s played as a Bear so far.

- Montez Sweat sacked Shough in the endzone for a safety.

- Dillon Thieneman had a nice interception early in the game.

- If I still had access to Tru Media (a wonderful platform) I would watch Jordyn Tyson’s full game against the Bears in the offseason to figure out why he didn’t do anything today.

- Chris Olave went 9-102 on 15 targets.

- Caleb Williams threw a block on 273-pound defensive lineman Colby Wooden, where Wooden gave him a pretty good pop, that helped spring Zavion Thomas for a 30ish yard end around. Williams took the hit on his throwing shoulder. Thomas also added a 40-yard reception where Williams threw an absolute dime.

- Williams interception came off a tipped pass at the line.

- Colston Loveland scored on a roll out to the flat where he leap frogged a defender on his way to the endzone.

- D’Andre Swift scored on a goal to go, underhanded shovel pass where Caleb Williams faked a roll out to his right, and underhanded it back across the formation to Swift. Interesting design.

- Rome Odunze ran a very good corner route and made a tough catch in the scoring zone. Rome is a former No. 9 overall pick, and this is the sort of play receivers taken with a 10 top pick make.

- Williams had an out of structure play to Sam Roush (who made a nice sliding grab) where very few quarterbacks could have managed that situation, in that way.

- I absolutely love that Salvon Ahmed is getting some reps.

- I point out the moments of positivity because the Bears are an important team to understand and I was very underwhelmed by their offensive performance overall, especially in the run game/ pass protection (I would go back and watch their center if I had endless time). I didn’t foresee struggles in either of those phases coming today. Maybe you could attribute some of the inconsistency to the weather, but in yet another game where it looked like Chicago was going to roll, as they were up 16-0, they were basically flat offensively for the rest of the day. I’ve been a major bull on the Chicago Bears over the past two years, but this is back-to-back very inconsistent offensive performances, this one coming against a mediocre defense.

- That said, Ben Johnson having Dennis Allen do whatever the hell Johnson usually does in the locker room, was a fantastic example of elite leadership, on many levels given that this came against the Saints, who Allen once coached.

Lions 31, Buccaneers 21
- I had a few people tell me last week that the Buccaneers defense is 1stor 2nd in defensive DVOA, and that was a prime example of why I don’t care about such things apart from using them as a baseline to find market inefficiencies. I hope things like this live forever.

- Jared Goff went 20 of 28 for 279 yards and two scores, while taking just one sack.

- Goff hit Jameson Williams for a long score on a deep post. This exact play is why Detroit’s personnel on offense is such a problem. Jahmyr Gibbs is a Marshal Faulk level talent. Amon-Ra St. Brown is an excellent route runner and ultra reliable player in the vein of prime Keenan Allen. Jared Goff is a guy that will shred defenses when he’s clean, like he did today. But that deep shot post to Williams, on top of everything else they have, is why they are one of the best constructed offenses in the NFL, because if you don’t play at least single high against the Lions, that kind of play is on the table all the time.

- Gibbs rushing production: 98 yards and 2 touchdowns on 23 carries, a big chunk of the yardage came in the second half.

- The Lions’ pass rush had a better game than I was expecting without Aidan Hutchinson.

- Baker Mayfield was sacked/ fumbled on his first play, I feel like he’s had a wild amount of fumbles this year

- I will watch some Emeka Egbuka film in the offseason because I’m not entirely sure what’s going on there. Mayfield has been bad this year, I don’t think much of the offensive coaching staff and while Egbuka isn’t a true headliner, I though he’d be a solid pro.

Giants 23, Jaguars 18
- I’m not sure I’ve ever seen a game with more plays reviewed, which added to how messy this one was.

- Opening kick off was returned to just past the 50, then after a failed run Trevor Lawrence delivered an absolute dime on a tight window, intermediate plus crosser, that was dropped on contact by Parker Washington (it was a very good hit by Holland, but a tremendous throw by Lawrence). Jacksonville had another drop (a much worse drop) on a perimeter, outside comeback on their first drive. Those plays foreshadowed many other missed opportunities on offense throughout this contest.

- DT DJ Reader had a great first drive, a great stop on a run on the first offensive play, a sack on the play after Chris Rodriguez busted a chunk play on 4th down. New York couldn’t have expected more from Reader this season.

- That first drive should have ended in a pop up pick in the endzone on 3rdand 20

- Lawrence had a really bad pick on the Jags second drive, caught by Deonte Banks.

- The Giants got cute with a very long hard count on their first snap off the above turnover, where they jumped themselves. Then they called an outside run out of the gun to Cam Skattebo against a defense with an elite front (he’s too slow to run outside against a team like this). Then McCarthy threw a dropped pick where he threw a check down to Skattebo that couldn’t have been more behind him. An absolute joke of a strategic sequence.

- I’m not sure why Jameis Winston was inserted into the offense to run the rest of a drive inside the 5-yard line, especially since McCarthy threw a very catchable deep ball to Malachi Fields, who didn’t come down with it, but drew PI to get them down there. Winston isn’t playing because he’s not reliable, bringing him in for four plays inside the 5, made absolutely no sense to me.

- Like him or not, JJ McCarthy made several very sharp throws in this game and a few savvy runs, against a real NFL defense.  I thought McCarthy did pretty well in pressure management against a tough front.

- That said, McCarthy did miss two downfield throws to Mooney, both pretty bad misses. New York also had a handful of drops.

- Count me as someone that doesn’t view Jaxson Dart as the automatic starter next season. That’s not really a pro McCarthy stance, as it is me thinking Dart isn’t anything special.

- After one of those missed deep shots to Mooney, on what was still looking like a potential scoring drive, Cam Skattebo lost a fumble that was returned 40ish yards the other way. McCarthy prevented it from being a touchdown, where the Jags ended up turning it over on downs.

- Skattebo is not an every week starter in the NFL, he’s a valuable rotation player long term.

- I’ve always been a big Abdul Carter guy, but I’ll say again that I’m not sure there is a more dangerous edge rusher in a one-on-one situation in the whole league and this was his best game as a pro to date. He was the Giants pass rush today with two sacks and double-digit pressures. Ironically, if the Giants still had an interior presence like Dexter Lawrence, their front would be a nightmare to deal with. That’s what is missing in this group.

- New York’s secondary had a great game, an absurd amount of defended passes.

- I thought the Washington touchdown that got reversed was a pretty obvious touchdown.

- This and the Denver game were the two shakiest games for Lawrence this season, and in this one he still threw for 300 yards and suffered a ton of drops. I wouldn’t overcount what happened in East Rutherford against Lawrence.

- However, his supporting cast on offense showed that they are very average today.

- For Jaguars fans, Jordan Davis did nothing and unfortunately, that’s not a surprise.

- In the interest of full disclosure, I wish next week was Daniel Jones’ last game in Indianapolis, that would have been appropriately poetic.

Eagles 19, Steelers 16
- This was a genuinely bad loss for the Steelers, especially since the Eagles were on top the whole way. The kind of loss where if they don’t make the playoffs, this game will be why.

- Aaron Rodgers was 17 of 20 for 95 yards at halftime. Pittsburgh just cannot throw the ball down field. Going into the year I was worried that Rodgers stayed one year too long. That wasn’t the case through the first half of the year, but this game and last week’s mess against the Bengals, not great.

- DK Metcalf was kicked out of the game in the second half for poking an Eagle in the eye. Metcalf had one reception for 2 yards on 4 targets.

- The Eagles’ front was impactful in both phases, with Byron Young having a very good game as a pass rusher.

- I was surprised that Jaylen Warren didn’t see more proactive passing game usage, I thought that was a pretty obvious lever to pull coming into this contest.

- Saquon Barkley scored early on a 38-yard run that could have been shut down near the line of scrimmage, but it was behind the Eagles still very strong left side.
-

- Joe Milton overthrew DeVonta Smith on what would have been a 70ish yard, gimmie TD. The Eagles went three and out on that drive.

- You have to give the Eagles credit for coming off their bye and stringing together a physical effort against a winning team.

Bills 26, Dolphins 9
- Greg Rouseeua created havoc in the first half with a number of disruptive reps and 2 sacks. I’d guess Miami had less than 50 yards of offense in the first half.

- In general, the Bills defense had a great game against a weak opponent.

- Buffalo went out of their way to air it out today, and I’d have to call what they did on the field underwhelming.

- I’ll continue to say that the Bills are more like a 12-5 team than a 9-1 group.

- The Bills converted on a 4th and 8, fake punt pass on a 30-yard throw, where basically all of it was in the air. I thought it was a ludicrous decision in the moment.

- Miami had two interceptions in the first half.

- Dolphins’ rookie quarterback Kyle McCord had a very tough day.

- I wasn’t crazy about the Jeff Hafley hire, but Miami has gotten better as the season has gone on and no one could be getting much more out of this team given the limitations of their roster.

Cowboys 51, 30 Titans
- Tennessee has the worst defense in football.

- Dak Prescott shredded the Titans in a 7 on 7 environment, he was close to perfect.

- CeeDee Lamb: 11-132-1, George Pickens 7-102-1. It seemed like Lamb had a ton of production early, Pickens had more late when the game was effectively over.

- Javonte Williams had another game that virtually any other running back in the league could have despite his 91 total yards and 2 scores.

- Kavontae Turpin (who I love) scored from 25 yards out on an outside run handoff, while lined up in the backfield, out of shotgun

- Carnell Tate had a 60ish yard TD reception on a freak play where he caught a slant, wasn’t touched, and busted it. (Cobie Durant thought he touched Tate while he was down).

- Cam Ward made a ridiculous 4th and long out of structure play late in this game for Tennessee’s final score, where he threw a pass completely across the field.

- I would treat this as more of a 20ish point type of output from the Titans offense, maybe even a touch less. Tate’s busted slant and Ward’s 4thand 8 garbage time scores were extreme outliers that led to 14 points.

- James Houston had a really impactful game as a pass rusher for Dallas, as did Quinnen Williams.

Panthers 35, Ravens 33
- In my Saturday preview I said that I could see this game being a shootout, but 68 total points in a very back and forth game was really something.

- From the Baltimore side, I thought Derrick Henry (13 carries for 94 yards and a score) and Zay Flowers (8 receptions for 97 yards) would have good games.

- Justice Hill’s 6 carries for 69 yards and a score, along with Rashod Bateman’s 2-67-1 line built off a 52 yarder, were more unexpected.

- The Ravens had four fumbles, losing 3

- Jacoby Brissett played very well considering that he was starting games for the Cardinals earlier this season.

- Jessie Minter’s defense has been a massive disappointment this season, he’s created zero margin. If anything, they’ve gotten worse.

- Chuba Hubbard ran for 120 yards and 2 scores on 27 carries.

- Bryce Young had a solid game, where Tetairoa McMillan went for a solid 6-71-1 and Jalen Coker had an underwhelming 4-47, including an early 35-yard reception.

- Overall this was a game where most scoring drives were finished with a touchdown, against two very underwhelming defenses.

Chiefs 34, Cardinals 7
- I’d guess the Chiefs ran 50 plays of offense in the first 35ish minutes of this game

- Another clinic from Patrick Mahomes against a bottom tier opponent: 27 of 39, 324 yards, 3 TDs. The great ones shred weak opponents just like this.

- Travis Kelce went 6-74-2

- While Kelce had a nice game, what I’m seeing out of the Chiefs since they acquired Josh Downs is they now naturally have a spread it around offense where each of their starting pass catchers, while none of them are true headliners, each of them does at least one thing well, with differentiation (Downs short area quickness, Xavier Worthy long speed, etc). I’m very curious to see what that looks like against Buffalo on Thanksgiving.

- Another really good game out of Emmet Johnson, who had around 150 total yards. I’m also curious to see what he’d look like with real run, against a real defense.

- George Karlaftis, who has always been one of my guys, had a very impactful game with two and a half sacks and I’d guess half a dozen pressures/ QB hits. He’s been a monster over the last three games.

Jets 27, Chargers 24
- Leave it to the Jets to win a battle that helps them lose the war (draft positioning). I say this because if the Jets can draft a new future at quarterback while keeping the rest of their premium picks, the could become a factor in a hurry with a new coach.

- Geno Smith had a great first half, 10 of 11, 112 yards, 2 scores, finishing 17 of 21 for 176 yards and 3 scores.

- Breece Hall had 20 carries while Braelon Allen had 16.

- The Chargers offense has been better the last two weeks, but their pass protection is still a problem, with Justin Herbert taking 6 sacks.

- No. 2 overall pick David Bailey had another spike game with two sacks and a number of other disruptive reps.

- Ladd McConkey: 5-37-2

Broncos 38 vs. Raiders 24
- Monster game from Jonah Coleman: 111 yard and 3 touchdowns on 24 carries.

- Troy Franklin dropped a deep shot in an indescribable manner, it looked like it hit him in the head while he was diving. Butt fumble level bizarre play that probably would have been a 50ish yard TD.

- Denver scored 38 points, but I was hoping for more out of their passing attack, because they are going to need more to go anywhere in the playoffs.

- Denver’s pass rush was impactful, with Jonathan Cooper having a very good game.

- Linebacker Alex Singleton had a ton of production in this contest, I’d guess around 10 tackles, a sack, a pass defended, at least one QB hit.

- Fernando Mendoza’s first two games remind me a lot of Joe Burrow, in the sense that you can just see that he can be a top 10 guy at the position. He’s mobile, he stayed even against two very good defenses in his first two starts, I hope they build the right way around him.

- Big game from Ashton Jeanty with 11 carries for 79 yards and 5-90-1 in the air, The score came on a 70ish yard reception, and he had a 50ish yard run, so most of his yardage came on two plays. It also looked like he got most of his work in the first half.

- The Raiders need a WR1.

Linebacker Nakobe Dean had a ton of production today.
- Madden wasn’t a very good movie, but Christian Bale was pretty freakin good as Al Davis. I thought the dynamic between Madden and Davis was the highlight of the movie. Some of the football specifics in it though were atrocious given who they were talking about.

Reminder that I do not edit this, as I get this out as soon as Sunday Night Football ends.

Parsons himself in 14 games last year: 12.5 sacks, 26 QB hits, 12 TFL, two forced fumbles, and 83 pressures, which led the NFL per Next Gen Stats. That was 38% of Green Bay's sacks in those games.

The on/off split inside those games told the same story. With him on the field, opponents averaged +0.05 EPA per dropback and took a sack on 7.1% of dropbacks. With him off the field (111 dropbacks), it was +0.14 and 3.6%.

Karl Brooks, Devonte Wyatt, Dani Dennis-Sutton and Edgerrin Cooper (in only four games) have 3 each. Their 29 sacks are tied for 7th.

Whether that is due to the NIL, coaching, this generation of player archetypes, or NFL teams leaning on veteran players more and giving rookies fewer opportunities early in their career

Could this blow up in my face with this 2027 draft class being heralded as "generational" (overused word, by the way)... maybe 

- But everyone loves propping up young, unproven, "potentially" high upside talent, when there is literal proven and tangible upside available at better prices 

KTC has become one of the worst websites for Dynasty values as well. It is highly, highly reactive to recent trends, that overreacts to incredibly small sample sizes or player injuries 

If I’m moving off picks, what am I targeting in return or what positional strategies am I looking to deploy?

1. Trade for affordable Year 2–4 WRs with real signs of upside 

Players that have shown elite upside, flashes of high-level talent, or are moving into a far better situation in the near future

1. This game, like the Texans, will be won or lost the Giants CB group. Jags WR's are very good led by Parker Washington. Giants can't pressure with 4 so they'll need to blitz and play man. Trevor Lawrence rips it downfield against man and CB's will need to cover well and get their heads around to find the ball

2. JJ McCarthy's best defense he has played in his career in the 2025 Atlanta Falcons (14th in EPA/Play). The Jags are 4th and also 2nd in scoring. Two things JJ will need to be. Patient but decisive against Jags zones and accurate against man. Jags CB's do a good job of baiting throws and will make you pay

3. There's not a lot of kicker options out there but there is options. Dominic Zvada is 8/14 in his last 5 games with 3 games of kicking sub 40%. Can't keep happening.

4. Giants need to either kick long FG's or go for it on 4th down. There's been way too many drives of the Giants punting from the opponents territory. Be mindful of it on 3rd down and understand you have an extra down.

5. Patrick Ricard barely played last week, but the Giants run game had success against a weak front. Jags run defense is much better with the addition of Jordan Davis who wrecked the Giants 2 weeks ago where the Giants had their most negative runs of the year. Ricard will need to play to help clean up IOL mess and hopefully spring big ones.

6. Ar'Darius Washington is coming off an amazing game and Andru Phillips is coming off of giving up a game winner. Against this Jags offense, I'd consider living in a 3 safety world with Washington playing nickel and Jason Pinnock playing the Strong Safety role.

7. Malik Nabers has had back to back sub par games with 2 big negative plays (dropped TD/Fumble) following his Player of the Month campaign. Jags will focus on him but quality targets need to be there. 

8. Coaches will often reward their players who set up others with games to get their stats. Abdul Carter has taken double teams, set up free rushers and pressured the QB into others big plays. Will the Giants try to reward Abdul Carter with some counting stats today? The lack of any other pass rusher makes it difficult but maybe you see some things that force 1 on 1's or put him over IOL which we haven't seen much of this year. 

9. Giants could go 1-3 (win over Colts) over the next 4 games and still likley make the playoffs, but a win over Jags, 49ers, or Seahawks would really stamp it. Increase your margin of error.
